buckets.label: Sense
buckets.hint: Getting the signal somewhere it can be read

buckets.label: Decide
buckets.hint: What gets said, to whom, when, and whether

buckets.label: Verify
buckets.hint: Was it true, and did it land

tasks.text: Setting up a weekly export of the intranet searches that returned no results
tasks.reasoning: Collection, not conclusion. Nothing has been decided and no meaning has been made. You have simply moved a signal from somewhere unreadable to somewhere readable. That is the whole of Sense, and it is the cheapest high-value thing on this list.

tasks.text: Sitting in on the regional operations call to hear what supervisors are actually worried about
tasks.reasoning: Unglamorous, unbillable, and the highest-fidelity instrument most communicators have. It is Sense because you're collecting raw signal in the place it occurs, before anyone has summarized it for you, which is where most of it is lost.

tasks.text: Turning four hundred unanswered search queries into a ranked list of what the workforce can't find
tasks.reasoning: The queries were Sense. Ranking them into a claim about what people can't find is Interpret. You have made meaning, and you could be wrong. This is the link where a model will happily theme forty tickets into five clean categories whether or not five categories exist.

tasks.text: Reading the pulse results and concluding the problem is one business unit's manager, not the policy
tasks.reasoning: A conclusion drawn from data, and a consequential one. It redirects the response from a policy rewrite to a management conversation. Interpret, and the most expensive place on the chain to be confidently wrong.

tasks.text: Telling the CFO that the "efficiency" framing will read as a layoff signal, and that the message should say what it means
tasks.reasoning: The clearest Decide card in the set, and the one most often misfiled. You aren't making the artifact and you aren't distributing it. You're changing what the organization will say. This is counsel, it costs credit rather than building it, and it is the work nobody's job description mentions.

tasks.text: Choosing which four of eleven competing items make this week's digest, and telling seven sponsors no
tasks.reasoning: Decide, though it feels like editing. The test: if you did this and produced nothing, would the organization be different? Yes, seven things didn't get said. That is a decision about the workforce's attention, and it is the everyday form of the work Module 3 turns into a kill list.

tasks.text: Drafting the CEO's all-hands script from a twenty-minute briefing
tasks.reasoning: Produce, and the canonical example. Note what makes it Produce rather than Decide: the twenty-minute briefing already contained the position. If you also changed what the CEO was going to say, that part was Decide and should be logged separately: the two happen in the same hour and get recorded as one.

tasks.text: Building the manager talking-points kit from the executive message
tasks.reasoning: Making an artifact from an existing decision. Module 9 argues this link is where AI's clearest return in the whole function sits (personalized manager enablement was economically impossible at scale and now isn't) but the work itself is Produce.

tasks.text: Scheduling the Slack post to land at 9am local in each region
tasks.reasoning: Distribute. Real work, genuinely necessary, and the link where the difficulty is tooling rather than craft, organizations that invested in a platform solved this years ago, and organizations that didn't are still doing it by hand at midnight.

tasks.text: Segmenting the benefits announcement so night-shift staff get the version about their enrollment window
tasks.reasoning: Distribute, and the version of it that AI genuinely improves, personalization at a finer grain than a channel platform could previously manage. It reduces the attention bill without reducing what anyone can find, which makes it one of the few uses that helps on Module 1's terms.

tasks.text: Confirming against the plan documents that the benefits summary is accurate before it publishes
tasks.reasoning: Verify, in its factual half. This is the check that used to happen for free because the person writing the summary had read the plan documents. A model writes it without having read anything, so the check has to be reinstated as a deliberate step, which is Module 5.

tasks.text: Finding out, three weeks later, whether anyone actually understood the enrollment deadline
tasks.reasoning: Verify, in its landing half, and the half that almost never has an owner. Note that it is also Sense for the next cycle: what you learn here's signal about what the workforce didn't understand, which is why the chain is worth drawing as a loop rather than a line.
